mtg_orbit_001.text: Okay. Everyone's here? Rahul, you're on mute. There you go.
Sorry, yeah. Can you hear me now?
Yes. Right. So this is the Orbit kickoff. We've got the October release to scope, owners to assign, and a few tech calls to make. I want to leave this call with dates.
Do we have the Meridian deck? I only saw the summary email.
I'll share it after. Short version: Meridian Bank is the launch customer. Three hundred field agents on the pilot, Android devices, patchy connectivity in the branches.
Patchy how? Like no network, or slow network?

Both. Some of the branches are literally in basements. That's why offline is in scope, which I'll get to. Scope first. The October release has three things in it: payments, offline mode, and onboarding. That's it. Nothing else gets in.
What about the analytics dashboard? Product's been asking for it since July.
Deferred. The analytics dashboard goes to November. I've already told them.
Okay, good. That takes a lot off the shell.
Release date. We ship on October 16th. That's a Friday. Meridian's pilot starts the week after.
Is that fixed, or aspirational?

Fixed. Their steering committee signed on it. If we miss it we miss the pilot window and we're waiting till January. Owners. Priya, you own the payments service end to end, including the UPI flow. Rahul, offline mode and the app shell. Sana, onboarding and anything a user touches.
Fine by me. I do want a decision on the payment vendor today though, I can't start without it.
Yeah, let's do it now. The options were Razorpay and PayU. What's your take?
Razorpay. Their UPI SDK is the fastest to integrate, we used it on the Lumen project, and their sandbox is decent. PayU I've honestly never touched.
I've only heard bad things about PayU's docs, for what it's worth.
Okay. Decision: payments go through Razorpay. Rationale, fastest UPI integration and we have prior experience with it. Priya, you're good with that?
Yes. I'll own the integration.
Then the UPI flow. Priya, when can you have it done? And I mean working end to end in sandbox, not a branch.
Let me think. If I have sandbox keys this week... the 24th. I can have the UPI flow done by September 24th.
The 24th. Written down. I'll get you the Razorpay sandbox keys by Wednesday, the 9th.
And I'll share the payments service API spec by Thursday the 10th, so Rahul can build against it.
Thursday's fine. I'll stub it until then.
Offline mode. Rahul, this is the scary one. How do we even approach it?
So, my proposal is local-first. SQLite cache on the device, a sync queue for writes, and the server reconciles when we're back online. It's boring, which is why I like it.
Does the sync queue need anything from the payments service? Like, do payments go offline too?
I honestly don't know yet. Let me spike it first.
Okay. Decision: offline mode is local-first, SQLite cache plus a sync queue. Rationale is the basement branches. We revisit payments-offline after the spike. Rahul, the spike. When?
Give me until the 18th. Offline mode spike done by September 18th, with a written recommendation on conflict handling.
Good. And the app shell?
The shell with navigation is quicker. I can have the app shell up by the 15th, assuming we pick the nav today.
Let's pick it. Sana?
I'd go with a bottom tab bar. Four sections: Home, Payments, Inspections, Profile. Everything is one tap away and users already know the pattern.
Agreed, a tab bar is the least work for me too.
Any reason not to? No? Okay. Decision: navigation is a bottom tab bar, four tabs. Rationale, discoverability, and it's the standard pattern.
I'll mock it up along with the onboarding screens.
Which brings us to onboarding. Sana, what's the shape, and when?

Five screens. Welcome, phone verification, PIN setup, permissions, and a quick tour. Nothing fancy, the field agents aren't going to read much. I can have the onboarding screens done by the 19th. That's a Saturday, but I'm out on Friday, so the 19th.
The 19th works. Rahul, you'll build them the week after.
Yeah no, that's fine.
Quick one. Platforms. Are we doing iOS at all?
Android first. iOS only if we have slack, which we won't. Meridian's devices are all Android anyway.
Can we at least flag iOS for November? There's that logistics prospect... sorry, never mind, that's not real yet.
Flag it. We'll see. Cadence. Standup every Monday at ten, this call. Design review when Sana needs one. Retro after we ship.
Mondays at ten. Got it.
One more. I'm doing a requirements call with Meridian on Friday the 11th. I'll bring back anything that changes scope.
Can you ask them about receipts? Whether they need a printed receipt or in-app is fine.
Will do. Anything else?
Not from me.
I'm good.
Same.

Then let me read it back. Scope: payments, offline, onboarding. Razorpay for payments. Tab bar nav. Local-first offline. We ship October 16th. Dates. Razorpay keys Wednesday the 9th, me. API spec Thursday the 10th, Priya. Meridian call the 11th, me. Shell the 15th and spike the 18th, Rahul. Onboarding the 19th, Sana. UPI flow the 24th, Priya.
That's right.
Great. Go build Orbit. See you Monday.
Later.
Bye.

mtg_orbit_002.text: Morning. Standup. Same shape as always: what you did, what's next, blockers. Then decisions since last time, then stale commitments. Priya, go.
Okay. Done: the payments service API spec went out Thursday the 10th, Rahul has it.
Got it, already stubbed.
In progress: the UPI flow. And... this is where I have bad news. It's going to slip.
How much?

The Razorpay sandbox doesn't fire the UPI collect callbacks reliably. I lost Thursday and Friday on webhook signature verification before I realised it was their side, not mine. So I need to move it to Friday. Friday the 25th, instead of the 24th.
One day. Okay. Is the 25th real, or is that hopeful?
It's real. I have a workaround, I poll their status API instead of waiting for the callback. It's ugly but it works.
Fine. UPI flow moves to the 25th. Noted. Blockers?
No. The sandbox keys came on time, thanks.
Rahul.
Done: the offline mode spike. Finished it Friday, so ahead of the 18th.
Nice. Verdict?

SQLite plus a sync queue works, like I hoped. Writes queue locally, replay on reconnect, a hundred records in under a second. The hard part is conflicts. When two agents edit the same inspection while offline.
Is that actually likely? Two people on the same record?
Meridian says agents share territories, so yeah, sometimes. So, new commitment from me: I'll bring a sync conflict resolution proposal to the design review on Wednesday the 16th.
Good. Shell?
Shell's on track for tomorrow. Tab bar is in, four tabs, it's ugly but it navigates.
Blockers?
One question, not a blocker. Does offline mode need to cover payments too, or just the forms and inspections? It changes the queue design a lot.
From my side I'd really rather it didn't. Offline payments is a nightmare.
I don't know yet. I asked Meridian on Friday and they didn't have an answer. Park it, I'll chase them. It stays open.
Okay. I'll design the queue so it can go either way.
Sana.
Onboarding screens. Three of five done, on track for the 19th. I'm changing the tour to three cards instead of five, like Aditya asked on the thread. The agents won't read five.
Good. Blockers?
Not a blocker, but Meridian sent over an accessibility checklist after your call. It's stricter than I expected. Minimum touch targets, screen reader order, that kind of thing.
Yeah, that's from their compliance people. Does it affect us?
Maybe. I want to check the tab bar against it on their five inch devices. I'll have the navigation accessibility review done for Wednesday's design review.
Wait, is the tab bar at risk? I just built it.
I don't know yet. Let me check before I say anything.

Fair. Wednesday, then. Okay, me. The Meridian requirements call happened on Friday the 11th. Three things came out of it. One, the pilot starts October 20th, three hundred agents. So the 16th really is the date. Two, decision: the pilot is Android only. iOS moves to November. Their devices are all Android, so there's no point.
Good, one less thing.
Three, receipts. An in-app receipt is fine, no printing. Priya, that was your question.
Perfect. That saves me a week.

Decisions since kickoff: the Android-only one, nothing else. Stale commitments: everything from kickoff is either done or has a date. The UPI flow is the only one that moved. And the offline payments question stays open. That's on me. Anything else? No? Okay. Design review Wednesday at ten. Bring the accessibility thing, Sana.
Will do.
Bye.

mtg_orbit_003.text: Design review. Sana has the onboarding screens and the accessibility review, Rahul has conflicts. Sana, start with the scary one.

Okay. So I went through Meridian's accessibility checklist with the tab bar on a five inch screen, which is what their field agents carry. Rugged devices, and they wear gloves half the time. The checklist says every primary navigation target has to be at least fifty-six dp, and navigation has to be a single landmark for the screen reader. Our tab bar, with four tabs on a five inch screen, gives us about forty-eight dp per tab. That fails. I tried three tabs, still forty-eight because of the labels.
Can we drop the labels? Icons only?
Then it fails their no icon-only controls rule. I checked.
So the tab bar is dead?
The tab bar fails Meridian's checklist. My recommendation is a side drawer. Full width items, as tall as we want, one landmark, and it scales when we add sections later.
I mean... I'm not thrilled. Drawers hide things. Discoverability was the whole reason we picked the tab bar at kickoff.
I know. But this isn't our preference versus theirs, it's a hard requirement in their contract. Fifty-six dp or they don't sign off.
Also, honestly, their agents will use this app eight hours a day. They'll find the drawer.
Yeah. Yeah, okay. Fair.

Alright. Let's be explicit about this, because we are reversing a kickoff decision. At kickoff we chose a bottom tab bar, for discoverability. We're reversing that. Decision: navigation is a side drawer. Rationale is Meridian's accessibility requirement, the fifty-six dp minimum touch target on five inch devices. That overrides discoverability.
Okay. Can I rip out the tab bar today?
Yes. When can the drawer be in?
The drawer's not hard. Side drawer implemented by Wednesday the 23rd.
The 23rd. And I'll send Meridian the drawer mockup for sign-off by Friday the 18th, so we don't get surprised twice.
I'll have the mockup to you tonight.
Now, I want to go further. If their checklist can kill the tab bar, it can kill anything. Sana, should it just be the baseline?
Yes. I was going to propose exactly that. Every screen gets checked against Meridian's accessibility checklist before we call it done.
Decision: Meridian's accessibility checklist is the baseline for every Orbit screen. Rationale, same as the drawer. It's contractual, and we'd rather find out in design than at sign-off.
Does that include the payment screens? Those are mostly Razorpay's SDK UI.
It includes anything we render. The SDK screens we can't change, I'll flag that to Meridian.
Okay. Onboarding screens, Sana.

Five screens, four done. Welcome, phone verification, PIN, permissions. The tour is the last one, three cards now. And applying the same reasoning as the drawer: the primary buttons on onboarding go to fifty-six dp, full width. Right now they're forty-eight and centred.
Same precedent, same answer. Decision: onboarding buttons are fifty-six dp, full width. The drawer decision is the precedent.
That doesn't change my date. Onboarding screens still done by the 19th, with the new buttons.
Good. Rahul, conflicts.

Right. Conflict resolution for offline mode. I looked at three options: last-write-wins per record, last-write-wins per field, and manual merge. Manual merge is the correct one and nobody will use it. Per record loses too much data. So I'm proposing last-write-wins per field, using the server timestamp.
Server timestamp, not device? Because device clocks on rugged Androids are a mess.
Server. The device sends its queue, the server stamps on arrival. Field-level means if I edit the meter reading and you edit the notes, we both win.
Any objections? Sana, from the UX side?
As long as the agent sees a this-record-was-updated toast, I'm fine.
Easy.
Decision: offline mode conflict resolution is last-write-wins per field, server timestamp. Rationale, it keeps the most data without asking agents to merge anything. Priya, anything on payments?

Quick update. The UPI flow is still on for Friday the 25th. The polling workaround is in, and Razorpay's UPI intent flow works in sandbox now. One risk. Meridian wants UPI autopay mandates for the subscription accounts, and Razorpay needs a merchant KYC step before mandates work in sandbox. I'm submitting that tomorrow.
How long does KYC take?

They say three business days. If it's more than that, I'll tell you by email, I won't wait for Monday. Also, the offline payments question is still open. I'm building as if payments need connectivity. If that changes, tell me this week, not next.
Noted. I've asked Meridian twice. I'll escalate.
Hey, are we still on for the drawer sign-off on Friday? Because if Meridian bounces it I want to know before I build it.

Friday. I'll push them. Okay, summary. Reversed: tab bar to side drawer, because of Meridian accessibility. New: the checklist is the baseline, fifty-six dp buttons, last-write-wins per field. Dates: mockup sign-off the 18th, me. Onboarding the 19th, Sana. Drawer the 23rd, Rahul. UPI flow still the 25th, Priya.
That's right.
Good review. Thanks, all.

mtg_orbit_004.text: Standup. Same shape: done, next, blockers. Then decisions since last standup, then stale commitments. Sana, you first this time.
Done: onboarding screens, all five, delivered Saturday the 19th with the fifty-six dp buttons. They're in Figma, Rahul has the link.
Yep. Started building them this morning.
Next: the payment screens review against the checklist, and I'm helping Rahul with the drawer states. Blockers: none.
Good. Rahul.
Done: tab bar is out, drawer is in on my branch. It should merge tomorrow, so on track for the 23rd. The offline sync queue is working on a real device now, replay and all.
Conflicts?
Last-write-wins per field is in, with the toast Sana wanted. Next: I want to demo the whole offline flow end to end next Monday, the 28th.
Put it down. Blockers?
Yes, actually. Test devices. I'm testing on my Pixel, which is not a five inch rugged thing you use with gloves. I need two of Meridian's actual devices.
I can lend you my old Moto, it's five inch.
It's not rugged and it doesn't come with gloves, but sure, thanks.
I have the Meridian call on Wednesday. I'll ask them for two test devices then.
Thanks.
Priya.
Okay. UPI flow. You've all seen my email from Thursday: it's Monday the 28th now, not the 25th. I'm confirming that here so it's on the record.
I saw it. That's the second slip, Priya. The 25th was supposed to be real.

I know. And the flow itself is done, the polling works, the one-time path works. What moved is UPI autopay, the mandates Meridian wants. Razorpay's merchant KYC for mandates is five business days, not three like they told me. It unlocks Thursday the 24th at the earliest, and I need two days to test mandates properly.
So the date isn't your code, it's their KYC.
Mostly. The 28th is honest. I'm not going to say the 25th and then email you again.
Okay. The UPI flow is Monday the 28th. That's the last move. If it slips again we cut mandates from the release, like I said in the email.

Agreed. If KYC isn't through by Thursday, I'll say so on Thursday. Also, repeating from the email so it's on the record: payments service deployed to staging by Friday the 25th, with the one-time UPI flow. So Rahul can test against a real endpoint instead of my branch.
That would help a lot.
Blockers?
Only the KYC thing, and the offline payments question, which is still open.
Right. Me. Meridian signed off the drawer mockup on Friday the 18th, no changes. Farah from their compliance team replied on the thread.
Oh, good.

Decisions since last standup. From the design review: the side drawer replaces the tab bar, Meridian's checklist is the baseline, fifty-six dp buttons, last-write-wins per field. Nothing new since Wednesday. One new decision today, though. Code freeze is Friday, October 9th. One week before release. Nothing merges after that except fixes.
Eleven days from the UPI flow to freeze. Tight.
It is. That's why the 28th is the last move. Stale commitments. The offline payments question has been open since the 14th. I'm closing it on Wednesday on the Meridian call, one way or the other.
Please.

Everything else has a date or is done. Rahul, your drawer is due the 23rd, you said tomorrow, so fine. The Meridian call is Wednesday the 23rd at nine, Priya's joining. We'll do a recap at ten for you two.
Okay.
Anything else? No? Go.
Bye.

mtg_orbit_005.text: Okay, recap of the Meridian call. Priya and I were on it. Rahul, Sana, you need to hear this before you write any more code.
That sounds ominous.
A bit. Good news first. Meridian is sending two rugged test devices, arriving Friday the 25th. Rahul, those are yours.
Finally. Thank you.
Second. The offline payments question is closed. Offline mode is for forms and inspections only. Payments require connectivity, full stop. That's their compliance team's position.
Thank god.
Great, that simplifies the queue. I'll strip the payment branch out.
Now the hard part. Meridian's compliance team joined the call. New people. Farah leads it, you've seen her on the drawer thread. They have requirements we didn't know about.
Such as?
Every payment attempt, successful or not, goes into an audit log retained for seven years. And all data stays in India. Data residency.
The audit log is fine, I log everything already, I just need to not delete it. Residency is fine too, we're in Mumbai.
And then, the vendor.
What about the vendor? Payments go through Razorpay. I've got their SDK wired into the shell already, that's done.
That's the thing. Meridian's compliance team mandates PayU. They have an existing merchant agreement with PayU. And they won't onboard a second payment provider. Not for a pilot, not for anything.
Wait. What? We decided Razorpay at kickoff. It's been Razorpay for two weeks.
We decided Razorpay because it was fastest for us. Nobody asked their compliance team. That's on me.
I pushed for Razorpay, so it's on me too. For the record, I did ask on the 11th whether they had a vendor preference, and the answer was no preference. Compliance wasn't on that call.
So the business side said one thing and compliance says another.
Yes. And compliance wins, it's their payment licence.
Can we push back? Is there any world where they accept Razorpay?
I asked. Farah said no, twice, politely. PayU, or no payments in the pilot.

Okay. So, what it costs. The UPI flow is behind an interface, I did that on purpose. Swapping the provider underneath is about a week. The polling workaround goes away, at least. PayU's callbacks apparently work.
A week on top of the 28th?
No. The 28th still holds for the flow itself, tested against the Razorpay sandbox because that's what I have. PayU sandbox integration I can have done by Thursday, October 1st.
That's eight days before freeze.
It is. It's doable. Mandates I'm less sure about on PayU, I'll know by Monday.
Alright. Decision: the payments service uses PayU. This supersedes the kickoff decision on Razorpay. Rationale, Meridian's compliance team mandates it and they won't onboard another provider.
Okay. I'll pull the Razorpay SDK out of the shell by Friday the 25th. It's two files, mostly.
Does PayU need anything from me?
Yes, actually. PayU requires an explicit consent screen before storing a payment instrument. Their copy, their checkbox. Can you design that?
Sure. Payment consent screen by Monday the 28th, checked against the checklist, obviously.
Good. Now the other new thing. Kestrel Logistics.
Who?
Second customer. A logistics company, a hundred and twenty drivers. They saw the Meridian demo and want the same app for delivery inspections. Meridian's CTO introduced them on the call.
Oh, so that's who Kestrel is. I kept hearing the name.
They want a pilot starting November 16th, and they need iOS, their drivers are on iPhones. So iOS in November is now a real thing, not a maybe.
Does Kestrel also have a compliance team with a vendor mandate? Asking for a friend.
Ha. I don't know. I'm doing a Kestrel discovery call on Wednesday the 30th, and this time I'm asking about compliance first.
Can I join that? Their onboarding will be different. Drivers aren't bank agents.
Yes, join.
So to be clear, nothing about Kestrel changes October.

Nothing. October is Meridian, Android, PayU. Kestrel is November. Let me read it back. Closed: offline is forms and inspections only. New requirements: seven year audit log, India data residency. Vendor: PayU replaces Razorpay. New customer: Kestrel, November, iOS. Dates. Razorpay out of the shell the 25th, Rahul. Consent screen the 28th, Sana. UPI flow the 28th, Priya. PayU integration October 1st, Priya. Kestrel call the 30th, me.
Correct. I'll email Razorpay's account manager tomorrow so they hear it from us.
One more thing. Can we write down why we picked Razorpay in the first place? Because in a month someone's going to ask, and I don't want to guess.
It's in the kickoff notes. Fastest UPI SDK, prior experience. Which turned out to be the wrong question. Okay. That's it. Retro next Wednesday.

mtg_orbit_006.text: Retro. Not the release retro, we haven't shipped. The three-week retro, because a lot happened. Format: where we are, what went well, what didn't, lessons. Then November, briefly. Where we are. Priya.
The UPI flow is done. Delivered Monday the 28th, one-time and mandates, tested against the Razorpay sandbox. The PayU swap is in progress, on track for tomorrow.
Rahul.
Drawer merged on the 23rd. Offline mode demoed end to end on Monday the 28th, on the Meridian devices, sync and conflicts, it held up. The Razorpay SDK is gone.
Sana.
Onboarding is built, Rahul finished it Friday. The consent screen was delivered Monday the 28th. Everything has been through the checklist.
And I did the Kestrel call this morning with Sana. More on that later. So. What went well.
Offline mode, honestly. The spike paid for itself. Deciding local-first on day one meant I never had to rethink it.
The checklist as a baseline. Once we said Meridian's checklist is the bar, every review got shorter. Nobody argued about button sizes again.
Putting the payment provider behind an interface. If I hadn't, the PayU switch would have been three weeks, not one.
Agreed on all three. What didn't go well. I'll start: the Razorpay decision.
Yeah. Can we talk about that properly? And actually, before that, I want to make sure I understand the drawer thing. Why did we choose the side drawer again?
Because the tab bar couldn't fit five sections, right? You wanted room for the Kestrel screens later.

No, that's not it. Kestrel didn't exist when we decided the drawer. It was Meridian's accessibility checklist. Fifty-six dp minimum touch targets on their five inch devices. The tab bar came out at forty-eight. We reversed the kickoff decision at the design review on the 16th, because of Meridian's accessibility checklist. Discoverability lost to the contract.
Oh. Yes. Sorry, I was conflating it with the Kestrel conversation. You're right, it was the fifty-six dp rule.
See, this is exactly my point. Two weeks, and we already have two different stories for one decision. Imagine in six months.

Which is a lesson. Hold that thought. Razorpay first. We chose Razorpay at kickoff because it was the fastest UPI integration and we'd used it before. We never asked Meridian's compliance team. Business said no preference, and we took that as the answer.
And I want to be fair to past us. No preference sounded like an answer.
It did. It wasn't. So, lesson one: confirm vendor constraints with the customer's compliance team before choosing a vendor. Not the business side. Compliance.
Agreed.
What else didn't go well. Priya, the UPI flow slips. Not blaming. Just, what do we learn?

Two slips. The 24th to the 25th was Razorpay's sandbox callbacks. The 25th to the 28th was their KYC for mandates. Neither was code. Both were vendor lead times I didn't know about. What I'd do differently: the second time it slipped, we should have cut mandates from the release right then, instead of giving it a new date. We got lucky the KYC came through.
I said that in the email and then didn't do it. So, lesson two: a commitment that slips twice gets a scope cut, not a third date.
That's going to hurt someday.
That's the point.
Can I add one? The drawer confusion just now. We make decisions in meetings and the rationale lives in someone's head.
Yes. Lesson three: record the rationale with every decision, in the meeting, in the notes. Not the decision alone. The why.
And who said it.
And who said it. Rahul, that's what the decision log is for, issue forty-two. The three lessons go in there too.
On it. Friday, like I said in the email.
Those are the three. Vendor constraints from compliance. Two slips means a cut. Rationale with every decision.
Is don't trust a sandbox a lesson or just a scar?

A scar. Okay. November, briefly. Kestrel call this morning. A hundred and twenty drivers, iOS, pilot starts November 16th. And I asked about compliance first. They have no vendor mandate, PayU is fine with them. Decision: the Kestrel pilot uses PayU too. One provider, one integration.
Their onboarding is different, though. Drivers get a vehicle check screen, not PIN setup. I'll explore a Kestrel onboarding variant by Wednesday, October 7th.
Good. Decision: the November release scope is iOS and the Kestrel pilot. Nothing else until October ships.
iOS means I need a Mac that isn't from 2019.
Put it in the budget request. Code freeze stays October 9th, release stays the 16th. No changes there.
PayU integration tomorrow, October 1st. Still on.
Good. I'll write up the retro notes with all three lessons and the rationale, and send them tonight, so by October 1st.
With the rationale.
With the rationale. Thanks, everyone. A good three weeks, mostly.
Mostly.
